metadata.title: Zurtex Verification Ledger
metadata.scope: Destination import baselines and airline carriage baselines for personal dog and cat travel. A production route result must also verify the origin export authority, transit jurisdictions, and operating flight segments.
metadata.disclaimer: Verified means the summarized baseline was traced to an official source on the verification date. It does not mean government approval, airline acceptance, or continuing validity after that date.

statusDefinitions.verified_official: Baseline claim checked against directly accessible official source material.
statusDefinitions.official_source_partial: Official source identified, but one or more exact production fields require a second human capture before publication.
statusDefinitions.do_not_publish: Unresolved or contradictory; not suitable for customer-facing output.

sharedEuropeanUnionSources.title: Current EU practical rules on travelling with pets

countries.name: United States
countries.label: Recent-travel and vaccination-origin sensitive
baseline: Dogs must follow the CDC dog-import pathway. The baseline includes a healthy appearance, minimum age of six months, a universally readable microchip, and a submitted CDC Dog Import Form.
The detailed pathway changes according to where the dog has been during the previous six months and whether its rabies vaccination record is United States-issued or foreign-issued.
State, territory, agriculture, airport, and airline requirements can add further conditions. Cats do not use the same CDC dog framework.
countries.engine: Ask recent-country history before showing the final dog pathway. Never apply the dog rules to cats. Create a separate Hawaii/Guam branch and an export-authority branch for the country of departure.

sources.title: Bringing a Dog into the United States
sources.authority: United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

sources.title: Pet Travel
sources.authority: United States Department of Agriculture APHIS

countries.name: Canada
countries.label: Scenario-driven CFIA pathway
baseline: Canada does not have one universal dog-and-cat checklist. CFIA requirements vary by species, age, origin, purpose, ownership, and whether the animal is accompanied.
The route result must select the applicable CFIA scenario rather than displaying a generic rabies statement.
Provincial, territorial, and airline conditions remain separate layers.
countries.engine: Model the CFIA decision tree as source-linked rules. Show the selected scenario and the questions that caused that selection.

countries.name: Great Britain
countries.label: Approved-route and dog-treatment sensitive
baseline: Great Britain means England, Scotland, and Wales. Northern Ireland follows a different framework.
The standard personal route requires compliant identification, rabies compliance, the correct travel document, a non-commercial declaration, and an approved route or transport company.
Dogs normally require recorded tapeworm treatment 24 to 120 hours before arrival. Breed restrictions and the carrier method must also be screened.
Non-compliance can lead to refusal, re-export, or quarantine.
countries.engine: Keep Great Britain separate from Northern Ireland. Calculate the dog tapeworm window backward from scheduled arrival, not departure.

sources.title: Bringing your pet dog, cat or ferret to Great Britain

countries.name: Ireland
countries.label: Current EU core plus dog tapeworm and entry checks
baseline: Ireland follows the current EU non-commercial framework for identification, rabies, origin-dependent titre testing, and travel documents.
Dogs require recorded treatment against Echinococcus multilocularis 24 to 120 hours before entry.
The result should identify the permitted entry route and the expected document and identity check.
countries.engine: Apply the shared EU ruleset first, then the Ireland dog-treatment and entry-point overrides.

sources.title: Pet travel
sources.authority: Government of Ireland, Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine

sources.title: EU rules on travelling with pets

countries.name: France
countries.label: EU core with age and dog-category overrides
baseline: France follows the current EU identification, rabies, titre, and document framework.
France does not use the young-pet exemption for animals that are not yet fully immune to rabies.
French Category 1 attack-type dogs are generally prohibited from import, while Category 2 dogs have additional ownership and control conditions.
countries.engine: Make breed screening mandatory for dogs. A breed conflict should appear before the general timeline.

sources.title: Travel: coming to France with your pet
EU rules on travelling with pets

countries.name: Germany
countries.label: EU core with federal and state dog restrictions
baseline: Germany follows the current EU identification, rabies, titre, and document framework and does not use the young-pet exemption for animals not yet fully immune.
Federal controls restrict import or transfer of Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Bull Terrier, and their crosses, subject to limited exceptions.
German states can apply additional dangerous-dog classifications and possession rules.
countries.engine: Run both the federal import screen and the destination-state rule layer. Do not label a route eligible until the state override is resolved.

sources.title: EU rules on travelling with pets

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.label: EU core with customs and origin-specific health overrides
baseline: The Netherlands follows the current EU identification, rabies, titre, document, owner-timing, and entry-control framework.
Young animals that have not completed the normal rabies-immunity period are not accepted through the standard route.
Animals arriving from Peninsular Malaysia can trigger additional Nipah-virus conditions.
Third-country arrivals must be presented for the relevant customs and identity checks.
countries.engine: Use destination-specific origin overrides. The Malaysia-to-Netherlands path should not look identical to another third-country route.

sources.title: Travelling from third countries to the Netherlands
sources.authority: Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority

countries.name: Spain
countries.label: EU core plus designated traveller entry point
baseline: Spain follows the current EU non-commercial framework, including identification, rabies, origin-dependent titre testing, travel documents, owner timing, and the ordinary five-pet limit.
A third-country arrival must use an authorised Travellers Point of Entry and undergo the required checks.
countries.engine: Validate the selected airport against the current authorised entry-point list. Entry-point data must be date-versioned.

sources.title: Travelling with pets
sources.authority: Spanish Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food

sources.title: EU rules on travelling with pets

countries.name: Italy
countries.label: EU core with confirmed national implementation
baseline: Italy applies the current EU non-commercial framework to owner-accompanied dogs and cats and distinguishes commercial or ownership-transfer movements.
Italy does not accept animals under the standard route until the normal rabies age and immunity conditions are satisfied.
The ordinary limit is five pets unless the event exception applies. Owner or authorised-person travel can be separated by up to five days when documented.
Italy does not require routine tick or Echinococcus treatment for entry.
countries.engine: Apply the EU core and Italy-specific young-pet and treatment overrides. Keep the commercial branch separate.

sources.title: EU rules on travelling with pets

countries.name: Portugal
countries.label: Date-versioned EU rules and airport-control timing
baseline: Portugal states that updated EU non-commercial pet-movement rules took effect on 22 April 2026. Results for travel after that date must use the current version rather than citing the replaced framework.
The practical core remains identification, rabies compliance, origin-dependent titre testing, the correct certificate, and owner or authorised-person timing.
Third-country pets can be refused and returned when health conditions are not met. Airport traveller-entry-point operating hours and transit circumstances can affect the arrival plan.
countries.engine: Version the rule set from 22 April 2026. Validate Lisbon and Porto entry-control windows and surface the operating-hour risk before booking.

sources.title: Entering Portugal from a country outside the EU
sources.authority: Portuguese Directorate-General for Food and Veterinary Affairs

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.label: Origin-risk and customs-channel sensitive
baseline: Switzerland generally requires compliant identification, rabies vaccination, and the appropriate passport or veterinary certificate for a non-commercial movement of up to five animals.
Higher-risk origin pathways can require a recognised rabies titre, waiting period, advance permit, and specified entry point.
Third-country arrivals can require declaration through the red customs channel. Young-animal and cropped-ear or cropped-tail restrictions must be screened.
countries.engine: Treat customs declaration as a journey step. Separate listed-origin, high-risk-origin, and young-pet branches.

sources.title: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets
sources.authority: Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office

countries.name: Norway
countries.label: Origin, entry-point, and dog-treatment sensitive
baseline: Norway requires compliant identification, rabies vaccination, and an accepted passport or certificate.
Higher-risk third-country routes require a recognised rabies titre and the applicable waiting period.
Dogs normally require recorded Echinococcus treatment 24 to 120 hours before entry, subject to limited origin exemptions.
Specified entry locations and advance notification can apply.
countries.engine: Calculate the dog treatment window from arrival and verify the selected entry point. Do not reuse an Ireland tapeworm rule blindly because exemptions differ.

sources.title: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets from third countries

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.label: Permit-led with a production editorial hold
baseline: The route is permit-led and requires an official health-document pathway. The microchip identifier must match the official records.
Vaccination, origin-risk, laboratory, age, number-of-pets, and breed conditions can alter eligibility and timing.

The official MOCCAE source is authoritative, but its detailed document was not fully retrievable during this audit. Exact permit validity, age, titre, and treatment fields must not be published from memory.
countries.engine: Keep this profile behind an editorial-publish flag until the current MOCCAE document is manually captured, compared, and signed off.

sources.title: Official pet import requirements PDF
sources.authority: UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment
sources.note: Official file identified; detailed extraction requires manual editorial capture before production.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.label: Origin-schedule and quarantine sensitive
baseline: Singapore classifies origins into Schedule I, II, and III, with materially different vaccination, rabies titre, permit, inspection, and quarantine pathways.
A compliant microchip, required vaccinations, dog licensing where applicable, import licence, customs process, and advance inspection booking form the common structure.

For relevant Schedule II and III routes, the rabies blood sample timing, accepted result, and waiting period are critical. Quarantine can range from none to home quarantine or animal-quarantine-centre detention depending on classification and eligibility.
The final parasite treatment and veterinary certificate operate in a short pre-export window.
countries.engine: Classify the origin first. The page should transform visibly between Schedule I, II personal, II non-personal, and III pathways.

countries.name: Hong Kong
countries.label: Special Permit, origin group, and quarantine sensitive
baseline: An AFCD Special Permit is required for import and for many transit or transshipment scenarios.

Hong Kong groups origins into Group I, Group II, Group IIIA, and Group IIIB. Compliant Group I and II animals can normally qualify for quarantine-free entry, while Group IIIA and IIIB routes use substantially longer and more complex quarantine pathways.
Mainland China moved to the revised Group IIIA pathway. Breed, hybrid-generation, manifest-cargo, quarantine-space, and licensing rules can all affect the plan.
countries.engine: Make group classification the first output. Quarantine-space availability must be shown as an operational dependency, not assumed from the regulatory minimum.

sources.title: Import of dogs and cats
sources.authority: Hong Kong Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department

countries.name: Japan
countries.label: Long-lead designated or non-designated origin pathway
baseline: Japan distinguishes designated regions from non-designated regions.

The ordinary non-designated pathway includes microchip identification before the relied-on rabies course, two qualifying rabies vaccinations, a recognised antibody test, a 180-day wait from sampling, advance notice at least 40 days before arrival, a pre-departure examination, and government certification.
Deficiencies can lead to detention for up to 180 days or refusal.
countries.engine: Calculate the earliest feasible arrival from the latest critical prerequisite. Show the 180-day clock as a dominant timeline element.

sources.title: Importing dogs and cats into Japan
sources.authority: Japan Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries - Animal Quarantine Service

countries.name: Australia
countries.label: Approved-origin, permit, cargo, and quarantine sensitive
baseline: Australia accepts dogs and cats through approved-country pathways. An animal in an unapproved country normally must move to an approved country and complete the required residence and preparation period there.

The process is long-lead and can include official identity verification, rabies vaccination, RNATT testing, import permit, additional testing and treatments, manifested cargo, a specified arrival pathway, and post-entry quarantine.
The government advises allowing at least six months. Breed and hybrid restrictions must be checked against the current guide.
countries.engine: Block unsupported origin states early. The timeline must be built from the official group-specific step-by-step guide rather than a single generic rule list.

sources.title: Step-by-step guides for bringing cats and dogs to Australia
sources.authority: Australian Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.label: Approved-origin, permit, quarantine, and rule-version sensitive
baseline: New Zealand uses approved-country and origin-category pathways under an Import Health Standard. Identification, vaccination, laboratory testing, import permission, transport, and quarantine requirements depend on the category.
A 2026 transition to updated import standards makes the intended arrival date a rule-selection input.

The current MPI guidance page was identified but could not be fully captured by the automated research environment. Exact transition dates and category-specific steps require a second human source capture before publishing.
countries.engine: Store effective-from and effective-until dates for each standard version. Keep the New Zealand result behind an editorial-publish flag until the source snapshot is complete.

sources.title: Bringing cats and dogs to New Zealand
sources.authority: New Zealand Ministry for Primary Industries
sources.note: Official page identified; exact 2026 transition details need manual editorial capture.

countries.name: Mainland China
countries.label: One-pet, origin, titre, and port sensitive
baseline: The personal route generally permits one dog or cat per passenger per entry.
The animal requires official quarantine or health documentation, rabies evidence, and a compliant microchip.

The default route can involve 30 days of quarantine. Exemption pathways depend on designated origin, accepted rabies-antibody evidence for non-designated origins, inspection outcome, recognised laboratory, and designated port.
The Chinese original and the current GACC lists control where an English summary differs.
countries.engine: Version the designated-origin, laboratory, and port lists separately. Show one-pet-per-passenger as a hard blocker before document steps.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.label: Origin category, permit, titre, and quarantine sensitive
baseline: Taiwan distinguishes recognised rabies-free origins from other origins and requires an import-permit workflow.
The result must evaluate residence history, microchip, rabies vaccination, recognised titre evidence, application timing, and whether the animal qualifies for a post-entry quarantine waiver.
Where detention applies, the ordinary facility pathway referenced by APHIA uses a seven-day period, with availability only arranged after required documents are accepted.
Pit Bull Terrier breeding and import restrictions must be screened. The original official veterinary certificate must be presented on arrival.
countries.engine: Implement the waiver logic as explicit conditions, including the 120-day and 20-to-120-day application branches. Never infer a waiver from a titre alone.

sources.title: Online Application System for Dog/Cat Import Permit
sources.authority: Taiwan Animal and Plant Health Inspection Agency

sources.title: Notes on Applying for Quarantine
sources.authority: Taiwan Animal and Plant Health Inspection Agency

countries.name: Thailand
countries.label: Prior permission, official certificate, and arrival inspection
baseline: Live animals are restricted imports and require prior permission from Thailand's Department of Livestock Development.
The traveller must use the official application process, carry the original veterinary health documentation, and report to the animal quarantine station for arrival inspection.
Exact vaccination, age, and certificate windows must be taken from the current DLD route documents for the origin and date, not from a travel blog.
countries.engine: Treat permission and arrival inspection as mandatory stages. Keep certificate timing in the source data so it can be updated without code changes.

sources.title: How to legally bring pets into Thailand

countries.name: Peninsular Malaysia
countries.label: DVS/MAQIS permit and origin-specific controls - editorial hold
baseline: Peninsular Malaysia uses the DVS and MAQIS permit framework. The personal pet route is expected to involve an ePermit, official veterinary documentation, compliant identification, vaccination evidence, and origin-specific quarantine or exemption conditions.
Sabah and Sarawak must be treated as separate jurisdictions, not as the same destination ruleset.

The DVS/MAQIS authority and permit route were verified, but the pet-specific condition tables were not fully extracted during this audit. Exact requirements must remain unpublished until manually captured and reviewed.
countries.engine: Split the three Malaysian jurisdictions. Keep Peninsular Malaysia behind an editorial-publish flag for exact pet-condition fields while still showing the official permit authority.

sources.title: Import and export permit information
sources.note: Authority and ePermit pathway verified; pet-specific condition tables require manual extraction.

countries.name: Philippines
countries.label: SPS import clearance with short final-document windows
baseline: The owner must obtain an approved Sanitary and Phytosanitary Import Clearance through the Bureau of Animal Industry.

The application uses vaccination and parasite records, microchip evidence, a pet photograph, and other supporting information. The ordinary personal clearance covers up to three dogs or cats and is valid for 60 days.

The pet must generally be at least 120 days old when applying. The official export permit or international veterinary health certificate must be issued within the final pre-departure window specified by BAI.
Compliant animals with complete documents can receive same-day veterinary quarantine release on arrival.
countries.engine: Calculate the SPSIC validity and final certificate windows independently. Warn if the planned arrival falls outside either window.

airlines.name: American Airlines
airlines.mode: Small eligible dogs and cats may travel in cabin on permitted routes. Ordinary checked-pet service is highly restricted; larger or other movements use American Airlines Cargo/PetEmbark where available.

airlines.name: Delta Air Lines
airlines.mode: Small eligible dogs and cats may travel in cabin. Cargo is a separately arranged pathway; do not assume ordinary passenger checked-baggage carriage.

airlines.name: Alaska Airlines
airlines.mode: Potential cabin, climate-controlled baggage-compartment, or Pet Connect cargo carriage depending on route and animal.

airlines.name: JetBlue
airlines.mode: Small eligible dogs and cats travel in cabin only. There is no ordinary checked-hold or pet-cargo option in the passenger product.

airlines.name: Air Canada
airlines.mode: Potential cabin, baggage-compartment, or AC Animals cargo carriage on eligible Air Canada-operated services.

airlines.name: LATAM Airlines
airlines.mode: Potential cabin or checked-hold carriage on eligible itineraries operated entirely by LATAM; cargo is a separate product.

airlines.name: Avianca
airlines.mode: Eligible dogs and cats may use cabin or checked hold within carrier limits; larger or ineligible passenger movements require cargo arrangements.

airlines.mode: Ordinary pets do not travel in the passenger cabin. Specialist hold or cargo arrangements are made through approved partners or IAG Cargo; recognised assistance dogs are separate.

airlines.name: Lufthansa
airlines.mode: Eligible small pets may travel in cabin; larger pets may use the aircraft hold; Lufthansa Cargo is available for other cases.

airlines.mode: Eligible small pets may travel in cabin, others in the hold or as cargo. Some destinations are cargo-only.

airlines.name: TAP Air Portugal
airlines.mode: Eligible dogs and cats may travel in cabin or hold on qualifying TAP-operated flights; other species or restricted routes use cargo.

airlines.mode: Eligible cats, dogs, and specified small birds may travel in cabin or aircraft hold subject to limits.

airlines.name: Emirates
airlines.mode: Ordinary dogs and cats do not travel in the passenger cabin. Eligible animals move in the aircraft hold or as cargo depending on route; falcon exceptions are separate.

airlines.name: Qatar Airways
airlines.mode: Dogs, cats, and birds may be accepted as checked baggage on many eligible routes or as cargo where the route, animal, connection, or aircraft requires it.

airlines.name: Etihad Airways
airlines.mode: Eligible cats and dogs may travel in cabin on selected Etihad-operated routes within strict limits; larger or ineligible pets require cargo.

airlines.name: Singapore Airlines
airlines.mode: Eligible dogs and cats travel as checked baggage on qualifying routes or via cargo. Ordinary pets do not use the passenger cabin.

airlines.name: Cathay Pacific
airlines.mode: Ordinary pets travel through Cathay Cargo rather than the passenger cabin or checked-baggage product. Direct booking eligibility is limited and specialist coordination can be required.

airlines.name: Japan Airlines
airlines.mode: On international services, ordinary pets travel in the aircraft cargo compartment under the airline pet service; passenger-cabin carriage is unavailable.

airlines.name: Korean Air
airlines.mode: Eligible dogs, cats, and household birds may travel in cabin or hold depending on weight, age, animal, and route.

airlines.name: EVA Air
airlines.mode: Ordinary accompanied dogs, cats, and eligible rabbits travel in the checked aircraft hold on qualifying routes. Passenger-cabin carriage is reserved for recognised service animals.

airlines.name: Qantas
airlines.mode: Ordinary pets travel through Qantas Freight, not in the passenger cabin. Specialist or approved pet-transport arrangements can be required.

airlines.name: Air New Zealand
airlines.mode: On eligible domestic services, pets can travel as checked baggage in the hold. International pet movements use cargo and approved pet-transport arrangements rather than the ordinary passenger product.
